newsitem.title: CHILE: Chile sees US-Latin American ties stable after vote.
newsitem.headline: Chile sees US-Latin American ties stable after vote.

text.p: Chile does not expect any major changes in the United States' relations with Latin America following Bill Clinton's re-election as president, said Foreign Minister Jose Miguel Insulza Wednesday.
"It is an election of continuity in which most (candidates) were re-elected in their posts and so I do not see major changes," Insulza told reporters.
Clinton won a decisive victory over Bob Dole in Tuesday's presidential vote, while the Republicans retained control of both houses of Congress.

Chile cannot expect immediate progress in talks on joining the North American Free Trade Agreement (NAFTA), which were stalled last year as the result of political difficulties in Washington, said Insulza.

"I don't think anything has changed for Chile in terms of free trade, nor for any other country in Latin America," he said. "We will have to wait to see the policy the (U.S.) government carries out in coming months."
Chilean officials had hoped talks on membership of NAFTA, which groups the United States, Canada and Mexico, would be resumed after the presidential elections.
Chile was invited to join the trade bloc at the Summit of the Americas in Miami in 1994, but talks stumbled after discussion of "fast track" legislation died in Congress.
"Fast track" allows Congress either to accept or reject trade agreements, but without the power to make any changes.

Chile officials have said they will not negotiate entry to NAFTA unless U.S. representatives have "fast track" powers, as they fear the accord would be picked apart in Congress under pressure from special interest groups.
